title: Molecular basis for thermoresponsive protein condensation in plants.
authors: Pathak, Sunita; Chakravarti, Ananya; Bersche, Carissa; Joseph, Jerelle A; Strader, Lucia C
journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
one_liner_zh: 该研究结合粗粒化分子动力学模拟与序列分析，揭示植物朊病毒样低复杂度结构域通过LCST型相分离感知温度，并实现凝聚阈值的预测与理性调控，直接聚焦无序蛋白介导的相分离机制建模，对IDR-PPI及AI/物理模拟方法有高度启发。
abstract: Plants continuously experience temperature fluctuations that shape their physiology, development, and survival. Yet, how plants sense and adapt to elevated temperatures at the molecular level remains only partially understood. Here, we uncover a sequence-encoded mechanism by which plant proteins directly sense temperature through phase separation. Focusing on prion-like low-complexity domains (PLCDs) in Arabidopsis thaliana, we combine cellular imaging, quantitative biophysics, and coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations to show that numerous PLCDs undergo reversible lower critical solution temperature (LCST)-type transitions. We find that PLCDs that are sufficient and necessary for phase separation confer thermoresponsive variability to full-length proteins. Sequence analysis and simulations reveal that thermoresponsiveness is encoded in compositional heuristics, with sufficient PLCDs enriched in aliphatic and aromatic residues, enabling accurate prediction and rational tuning of condensation thresholds. Engineered variants with altered sequence composition exhibit predictable shifts in thermoresponsive behavior, confirming a direct, sequence-level encoding of temperature sensitivity. Our findings establish LCST-driven phase separation as a fundamental mechanism of thermoresponsiveness in plants and provide a molecular framework for designing synthetic biomolecules with programmable temperature responses.
abstract_zh: 植物持续经历着影响其生理、发育和生存的温度波动。然而，植物在分子水平上如何感知和适应升高的温度仍仅被部分理解。在此，我们揭示了一种序列编码机制，通过该机制，植物蛋白通过相分离 (phase separation) 直接感知温度。聚焦于拟南芥 (Arabidopsis thaliana) 中的朊病毒样低复杂度结构域 (prion-like low-complexity domains, PLCDs)，我们结合细胞成像、定量生物物理学和粗粒化分子动力学 (molecular dynamics) 模拟，表明众多PLCDs经历可逆的下临界溶解温度 (lower critical solution temperature, LCST) 型转变。我们发现，足以且必需用于相分离的PLCDs赋予全长蛋白热响应变异性。序列分析和模拟揭示，热响应性编码于组成性启发式规则中，富含脂肪族和芳香族残基的充足PLCDs能够实现凝聚阈值的准确预测和合理调节。具有改变序列组成的工程化变体表现出热响应行为的可预测性转变，确认了温度敏感性的直接序列水平编码。我们的发现确立了LCST驱动的相分离作为植物热响应性的基本机制，并为设计具有可编程温度响应的合成生物分子提供了分子框架。
